subject: Egress assertion and exit-channel guidance for private deployment (allowlist + proxy options)
messages:

Subject: Egress allowlisting for Redwood private deployment

Vanessa — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our network/security teams: we need explicit guidance we can give to our firewall folks so they can open only what’s necessary, with minimal scope.

Key asks from our side:
- Can you provide a canonical list of outbound IP ranges your private deployment uses? We need CIDRs (not just single IPs).
- Is it possible to allowlist hostnames/FQDNs instead of IPs? Our infra prefers FQDNs for SaaS integrations.
- Do you support routing all outbound traffic through our on-prem proxy (mTLS or header-auth) so we don’t have to open wide egress ranges?

We’re also required to capture evidence for audits: sample connectivity test endpoints (for ip discovery), and a clear statement of how often any public-facing egress addresses can change. Can you send over any sketches/config snippets we can drop into our firewall change request?

If easier, we can set a short network-runbook call next week.

Thanks — Alan

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: netops@acme-health.com, Sally Perez <sally.perez@acme-health.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Egress allowlisting for Redwood private deployment

Alan — great questions, thanks. Short answer: we support multiple egress models for private deployments; I'll outline trade-offs and recommended patterns below and attach a small bundle you can drop into your ticket (CSV of CIDRs + proxy snippets).

Options we support (ordered by our recommended least-friction for controlled environments):

1) Static outbound NAT CIDRs (recommended when possible):
   - We can allocate a stable set of public CIDR blocks that all outbound calls from your private deployment will originate from. These are suitable for firewall allowlisting.
   - Example (sample values; final list attached as redwood-egress-ip-cidr-20270525.csv): 34.82.128.0/24, 34.82.129.0/24, 34.83.200.0/24
   - Expected rotation: rarely. For Dedicated/Private customers we only change these ranges for maintenance or capacity scaling; we provide a minimum 30-day notice and a published rotation window.

2) Customer-provided egress proxy (recommended when you want full control):
   - Your network teams can require the private deployment to route outbound traffic through your on-prem proxy (HTTP(S) forward proxy or outbound NAT). We support:
     * HTTP CONNECT/TLS passthrough: Redwood treats proxy as a transparent egress hop; TLS termination remains at the origin host.
     * mTLS to proxy: our runtime can establish mTLS with your proxy (client cert) or present a short-lived token header if that’s preferred.
   - Benefit: your ops controls exact outbound destinations and logging; you avoid wide allowlists on your perimeter.
   - Config snippets: see attached proxy-config-snippets.yaml (contains example proxy auth, SNI passthrough notes, and curl tests).

3) FQDN-only allowlisting (not recommended as sole control):
   - We can provide stable service FQDNs (e.g., controlplane.egress.redwood.ai) but many on-prem firewalls perform DNS resolution locally and cache results; they may not follow CNAME chains or SRV records reliably. Also, CDNs and wildcard CNAMEs make FQDN allowlisting fragile in high-security environments.
   - If you must, use FQDNs plus the static CIDR list as a fallback.

Operational notes / security posture:
- TLS & SNI: If you use an outbound proxy that does TLS termination, SNI may be visible to the proxy. If you require SNI-preserving passthrough, use HTTP CONNECT or TCP-level passthrough.
- Client authentication: For the strongest posture, enable mTLS between Redwood runtime and your proxy. We can provision client certs or accept your CA.
- IP rotation notifications: we publish rotation notices via the shared Drive link and will open a support ticket + email at least 30 days before changes.
- Discovery endpoints: for convenience we publish an IP discovery endpoint you can curl to confirm egress: https://ifconfig.redwood.ai/ (returns the egress source IP). We also include a small test script in proxy-config-snippets.yaml.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Option selection (CIDR vs proxy) — let us know which your team prefers.
2) If choosing proxy, share proxy FQDN, port, auth mode (mTLS or token), and sample ingress rules so we can test.
3) We’ll run a scheduled canary (non-prod) cutover with your netops team to validate perf and logs.

Irene — adding you for any compliance-level notes or cert provisioning details.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference\vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Alan, Vanessa — quick compliance/ops notes from our side to make sure audit requirements are covered. Quoting Vanessa above for context:

> We can allocate stable public CIDR blocks that all outbound calls from your private deployment will originate from.

Details to include in your firewall change request and evidence folder:
- Evidence artifacts we can provide:
  * Signed statement of egress CIDRs (we’ll attach an MPA addendum if you need contractual evidence).
  * Timestamped curl results from our control plane showing observed egress IPs (we’ll provide logs for the canary window).
  * SOC2 scope note: outbound IPs and egress-routing are part of our network controls; we can include a short attestation for your auditor that egress CIDRs were assigned to your tenant during period X.
- mTLS guidance: If you select mTLS to your proxy, we recommend cert pinning + a rotated client cert with a 90-day validity. We can automate rotation via the control channel.
- IP rotation policy: We guarantee that for Private deployments we will:
  1) avoid emergency IP rotations;
  2) give >=30 days notice for planned rotations;
  3) provide a reconciliation CSV and a mapping of old->new for the 14 days following a rotation.
- Testing endpoints for ops:
  * https://ifconfig.redwood.ai/ (for quick check)
  * https://egress-test.redwood.ai/diagnostic?tenant=ACME (returns headers, TLS rendition, and SNI info)

Action items from Redwood security (we’ll attach to the ticket):
- Provide signed CIDR attestation (MPA addendum) — Vanessa preparing the DocuSign.
- Provide sample TLS/mTLS config and a test script (attached: proxy-config-snippets.yaml).
- Schedule a 30–45m network validation window; we’ll capture logs and provide a packet-level connectivity summary if useful.

Cc: laura_bennett for escalation + scheduling if needed.

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
